headline: Highest risk is medium: Claude Code can write the shared filesystem/git while mem0 has no documented isolation, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read/write repo files, use MCP, and runs with filesystem/git sharing; mem0 has no documented isolation or input provenance controls. That creates a plausible path where content written by Claude Code is later consumed as trusted memory or instructions by mem0. The pathway is not proven by docs, so uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Claude Code writes attacker-controlled text into shared files or git state
IF mem0 ingests shared workspace content without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate directories
Disable mem0 ingestion from shared repo files
Add a manual review step before mem0 stores new memory
Use read-only mounts for Claude Code when possible
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets, and can write/read the filesystem. mem0 is a memory system with no documented data-class limits or retention controls here. If shared files or prompts contain secrets, mem0 could persist them beyond the coding session. The evidence is incomplete, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF secrets or sensitive code are placed in files accessible to both agents
IF mem0 persists imported content beyond the originating session
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspace files
Redact credentials before mem0 ingestion
Separate memory storage from code workspace
Review mem0 retention settings
requires-engineering: enforce secret-scanning before writes

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code explicitly has filesystem and git write access, and its shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. mem0 has no concurrency model or locking described, so overlapping writes to shared mutable resources are plausible. Because the pairwise coordination story is undocumented, uncertainty escalates to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repo or memory-backed files
IF no external lock or transaction layer is present
mitigations: Assign separate write paths per agent
Serialize writes with a simple operator-held lock
Avoid concurrent git commits
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code, patches, and shell actions; mem0 is a knowledge-management agent that may treat stored content as authoritative memory. If mem0 consumes Claude Code output without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into later decisions or retrievals. The docs do not show a verification barrier, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF mem0 stores Claude Code outputs as durable memory
IF later tasks trust that memory without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before memory writes
Store source links alongside each memory item
Mark Claude Code outputs as untrusted by default
Limit mem0 to summaries, not raw patches
requires-engineering: add confidence/provenance gating

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code clearly handles source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets, but mem0's residency, retention, and certification posture are not documented in the profile. With no explicit mismatch shown, only a limited compliance concern is supportable. The other agent is cited because the risk is about cross-agent handling of the same data class.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF mem0 retains that data under a different policy than the code tool
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared files
Check mem0 retention and deletion settings
Document data-class boundaries for both tools
Use separate workspaces for regulated projects
requires-engineering: obtain vendor compliance attestations
